title: How do you deal with sprite sheets effectively?
author: Appropriate-Value610
selftext:
Hey everyone, I’ve been having lots of fun building a simple iOS 2D cartoon style skateboarding game. My workflow is pretty basic at the moment:  
\- Claude Code for almost everything  
\- Using Nano Banana Pro to generate sprite sheets and then feed them into Claude Code to create animations/movements

My challenge is: I want to create animation for skateboarding tricks. However, when Claude Code process the sprite sheets and put the animation together, there are always some weird glitches/cuts/shadows/etc which makes the animation look bad.

I tried to create each image separately (instead of using sprite sheets), and sometimes the outcome is better, but then I hit an image consistency challenge sometimes (e.g: character, or board may look slightly different), which again impacts the quality of my final animation.

I’m considering to try GPT 2 Images model, and see how it goes.

What’s the ideal animation workflow you recommend in my case?

Thanks

comments.author: Themadhatter_Laoni
comments.body: Same here, it's a nightmare to maintain the sprites consistency. Honestly I just take my asset on hitch.io now...

replies.author: Appropriate-Value610
replies.body: It’s really hard! Can you expand a bit more on what do you mean by taking your assets to hitch.io? How’s your animation workflow?

comments.author: kingkong_siu82
comments.body: The glitches and identity drift are the usual tax when you generate a sheet then stitch it in code. I built Motif (https://trymotif.app/) for this iOS path: one character image in, consistent frames out, then an .imageset plus a small SwiftUI Motif Sprite so you are not hand-fixing Nano Banana cuts. Sprite Sheet is a 12-frame loop; Motion AI if a trick needs a longer clip. It will not give you 8-direction combat sheets, but for a cartoon skate character's idle/trick loops it stays on-model a lot better.

comments.author: Nasilbitatbirakti
comments.body: You can't mass produce them consistently. What I'm doing is a combination of rigging, shaders and minimal amount of spritesheets where it's inevitable such as facial expressions.

comments.author: Illustrious-Lake2603
comments.body: Im experimenting with a workflow using H3 image start and end frames being the still image of the sprite. Then you animate it, take the frames you want, clean them up and use that as the sprite sheet. So far the animations look good to me. I havent tested in game yet.
